title: Supply Chain Resilience Assessment: Identifying Single-Source Dependencies, Lead-Time Vulnerabilities, Inventory Buffer Adequacy, and Supplier Diversification Roadmap
subtitle: Supply Chain Resilience Report — Single-Source Dependencies, Lead-Time Vulnerabilities, Inventory Buffer Adequacy & Supplier Diversification Roadmap

document_brief.narrative_theme: This report quantifies where single-source dependencies and long lead times create the largest service-risk exposure, tests whether current inventory buffers can absorb disruptions, and lays out a phased supplier diversification roadmap to reduce risk while protecting cost and quality.

sections.heading: Single-Source Dependency and Lead-Time Vulnerability Hotspots (Q2 2026 Baseline)
key_facts: As of 2026-04-15, 14 of 52 active SKUs (26.9%) are single-sourced and represent $38.4M in annual spend.
The longest end-to-end lead time is 18 weeks for the MCU-32 microcontroller sourced from Apex Semiconductors (Taiwan).
Custom Resin R-7 from NorthChem is single-sourced and has a 12-week lead time with a 92% on-time delivery rate in the last 12 months.

sections.heading: Inventory Buffer Adequacy and Supplier Diversification Roadmap (H2 2026–2027 Execution Plan)
key_facts: Finished-goods safety stock is 21 days versus a required 35 days to cover a 4-week supplier outage for the top 10 SKUs by revenue.
A 2026-09-30 target is set to qualify a second source for MCU-32, reducing single-source spend concentration from 41% to 25% in the Electronics category.
The roadmap funds $1.8M in supplier qualification and tooling from 2026-07-01 through 2027-03-31 to add 6 dual-sourced components.

structure.heading: Single-Source Dependency and Lead-Time Vulnerability Hotspots (Q2 2026 Baseline)
text_content: **Single-Source Dependency and Lead-Time Vulnerability Hotspots (Q2 2026 Baseline)**

15, 14 of 52 active SKUs (26.9%) are single-sourced and represent $38.4M in annual spend. This concentration creates strategic exposure across commodity, component, and finished-goods categories; four of those SKUs exceed $2.5M each in yearly purchasing. Immediate risk classification assigns these SKUs to high-priority monitoring and contingency planning. Governance will review supplier concentration quarterly and report mitigation progress monthly to the Executive Risk Committee.

The longest end-to-end lead time identified in the Q2 2026 baseline is 18 weeks for the MCU-32 microcontroller sourced from Apex Semiconductors (Taiwan). Extended lead time creates inventory and capacity strain through forecasting cycles and elevates the cost of expedited logistics; this SKU is flagged for dual-sourcing evaluation and safety-stock reassessment.
incentives to protect production continuity; alternative-material trials are scheduled in H2 2026.

structure.heading: Inventory Buffer Adequacy and Supplier Diversification Roadmap (H2 2026–2027 Execution Plan)
text_content: **Inventory Buffer Adequacy and Supplier Diversification Roadmap (H2 2026–2027 Execution Plan)**

Current finished-goods safety stock is 21 days versus a required 35 days to cover a 4-week supplier outage for the top 10 SKUs by revenue. This 14-day shortfall exposes revenue-critical items to stockout risk and necessitates immediate buffer replenishment, prioritizing SKUs with highest margin and customer-service impact. Inventory planning will adjust reorder points and expedite inbound logistics where economically justified.

A targeted qualification is scheduled to qualify a second source for MCU-32 by 2026-09-30, reducing single-source spend concentration in the Electronics category from 41% to 25%. Procurement will use formal RFPs, technical evaluation, and dual-sourcing pilots to validate performance, compliance, and cost neutrality before cutover with quarterly reviews.

The supplier diversification roadmap allocates $1.8M in supplier qualification and tooling from 2026-07-01 through 2027-03-31 to add 6 dual-sourced components. Milestones include supplier qualification completion, tooling sign-off, sample validation, and production ramp; governance will report progress monthly to the Executive Supply Resilience Committee.
